full_details: At Paul's you found a book on a board, new, small, and cheap. The True Tragedie of Richard Duke of Yorke, as acted by the Earl of Pembroke his servants, printed for Thomas Millington, 1595. Your York-and-Lancaster play, another company's name, no author's. You opened it standing. It fell at "Oh Tygers hart wrapt in a womans hide". You read two pages. They were yours, mostly, with holes. You did not buy it. Michael Drayton, at your elbow, asked if it was yours. You said it was. He asked if they paid. You said they paid somebody. On the way to the Theatre you said your name is on two poems and a tax, and not on a play, and asked whose the plays are. At home the garden was still open. You did not finish it. Where a parliament would be, the sheet is blank. You did not write it. At the Theatre the bag was not shut. John Heminges would not name a share. Last Saturday was 36s, and that was last Saturday. The Rose's bill for today is marked paid, the Revels' fee, and no sum was added. Titus went this afternoon. You were not in it.
one_sentence: You found your old play on a stall under Pembroke's name, added a few lines to the garden, and came away from John's open bag.
title: Found the York book at Paul's
